title: LLM-guided experiments identify three phases unique to the ternary Co–Al–Ge system
summary: Researchers used an LLM to plan iterative composition measurements and experimentally mapped the Co–Al–Ge phase diagram at 900 °C. The domain-specific aLLoyM model directed early measurements into compositionally complex interior regions, enabling the earliest discovery of all three novel phases reported to form only in the ternary system; the general-purpose LLM strategy found more phases in fewer cycles. This is an arXiv preprint and the finding is bounded to this experimental phase-diagram study.
ai_technology: aLLoyM domain-specific large language model and general-purpose LLM experimental planner
organization: National Institute for Materials Science; Tohoku University; University of Tokyo

evidence.tested: Researchers used an LLM to plan iterative composition measurements and experimentally mapped the Co–Al–Ge phase diagram at 900 °C.
evidence.unknown: This source is an arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal publication as of the checked record. The source abstract supports the reported ternary phase-diagram result and three phases described as novel and ternary-only, but does not provide their formulas or independent replication evidence in the abstract. The discovery is a bounded materials result, not a claim that every phase in the full ternary diagram has been exhaustively mapped.
evidence.ai_role: LLMs selected compositions for each cycle in a closed loop with high-throughput synthesis and X-ray diffraction phase identification. The original abstract specifically attributes earliest discovery of all three newly reported ternary-only phases to aLLoyM-guided initial measurements; a general-purpose LLM chose a textbook-like measurement strategy that efficiently found a larger number of phases in fewer cycles.
